Hi Sara / Olga — I reviewed the DPA draft HearthBank sent and sketched out three items we typically raise during enterprise deals. I wanted to put these on the thread so we can be explicit in the redline session: 

1) Data retention windows — Redwood supports per-tenant retention controls. We will propose: default 13 months for non-sensitive logs, 6 months for request-level telemetry, and customer-controlled data retention for processed outputs. If you require shorter windows we can scope an archival/auto-delete policy.
2) Subprocessor disclosure cadence — we publish a rolling list and provide 30-day notice for major additions; we can include an SLA for notification to a named HearthBank contact.
3) Export & deletion SLA — our standard is export within 72 hours on request and deletion confirmation within 30 days (longer if legal hold applies). For financialregulated customers we can discuss faster SLAs as a commercial concession.

I attached a first pass redline (DPA_redlines_hearthbank.docx). For the MAP session, can procurement confirm the earliest internal legal window for a live review? If procurement can commit 4/21–4/23 for a redline call (30–45m) that lines up with the timeline Olga proposed.

Thanks — Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sara — quick technical notes to prep for the redline call and to address the retention/export questions you raised.

Storage & residency:
- Primary region: us-west-2 (default). We support per-tenant residency in eu-west-1 for customers who purchase a residency add-on. Backups are encrypted and replicated within the same region unless a cross-region vault is requested.

Deletion & audit proof:
- Deletion is performed via our control plane and emits an immutable audit event (unique request id). We can provide an export of the audit event (JSON with timestamp + request id) as proof of action. For customers requiring signed assertions, we can produce a signed confirmation PDF from our ops team within 72 hours post-deletion (commercial add-on in strict regulatory cases).

CAIQ clarifications (high level):
- We filled out the CAIQ spreadsheet and added hyperlinks to SOC 2 control mappings (see CAIQ-responses-hearthbank.xlsx)
- A few items will need manual evidence: key rotation policy copy, penetration test summary, and backup testing cadence — we can surface those in the live call

I'll join the 4/22 call and demo the retention controls for a 10–15 minute walkthrough.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
